"a mobile real-time tactics (RTT) game heavily inspired by the single-player campaign and story-driven structure of Company of Heroes.
1. Core Concept @COMMENT_BODY@ Setting
• Genre: Squad-based Real-Time Tactics (RTT) with a strong, cinematic single-player narrative campaign.
• Setting: World War II (specifically focusing on a gritty, grounded, boots-on-the-ground infantry and armor campaign, similar to the Normandy invasion or the Liberation of Europe).
• Tone: Band of Brothers-style emotional storytelling, focusing on the camaraderie, sacrifice, and survival of a specific company of soldiers across interconnected missions.
2. Mobile-First Gameplay Mechanics
• Tactical Combat: Retain the core Company of Heroes mechanics—directional cover (green/yellow/red), squad suppression/pinning, flanking, destructible environments, and combined arms (infantry, support weapons, light vehicles, and tanks).
• Mobile Controls @COMMENT_BODY@ UI: Design an intuitive touch-screen control scheme. Include smart pathfinding, auto-cover seeking when moving near walls/craters, a tactical pause (or slow-motion) feature for issuing complex orders on a small screen, and a clean, non-cluttered HUD.
• Session Length: Structure campaign missions into 10-to-15-minute chapters with mid-mission checkpoints to fit mobile play habits.
3. Story @COMMENT_BODY@ Campaign Structure
• Narrative Delivery: Outline a 10-mission story arc following a single platoon. Explain how the story is told between and during missions (e.g., animated comic-style cutscenes, radio chatter, in-engine scripted events, and soldier journals).
• Persistent Squads: Design a system where squads carry over between missions, gaining veterancy, persistent injuries, and unlockable gear, making player losses emotionally impactful.
4. Tech Stack @COMMENT_BODY@ Monetization
• Engine: Recommend the best engine (e.g., Unity or Unreal) and outline the core technical systems needed (Fog of War, cover grid system, squad AI state machines).
• Monetization: Propose a fair, player-friendly monetization model suitable for a story-driven mobile game (e.g., premium upfront, free first chapter + full game unlock, or cosmetic/commander DLCs—strictly no pay-to-win).
Deliverables Needed:
1. A high-level Game Design Document (GDD) covering the points above.
2. A detailed breakdown of the touch-control UX and cover/suppression mechanics.
3. A 3-act narrative outline for the campaign with 3 sample mission concepts.
4. Basic C# (Unity) pseudocode/architecture for a Squad Cover @COMMENT_BODY@ Suppression System.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile-first World War II real-time tactics campaign prototype based on the supplied GDD concept.
- Deliver a polished battlefield demo with controls, combat, cover, suppression, campaign dossier, and narrative framing.

## Requirements
- Strongly inspired by *Company of Heroes* single-player campaign storytelling.
- Mobile-friendly touch controls, tactical pause, compact HUD, cover, suppression, and 10–15-minute mission structure.
- 10-mission, 3-act campaign concept with persistent squads and embedded narrative.
- Fair monetization; Unity and technical architecture guidance requested.
- Basic C# pseudocode/architecture for squad cover and suppression.
- Note reasonable assumptions made and save screenshots for visual checks.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game as a browser-based HTML/CSS/JavaScript prototype rather than Unity C# code.
- Assumed a 1944 Normandy setting and an initially playable Chapter 1 mission.
- Included campaign and field-manual information directly in the mission dossier.
- Used a premium/full-campaign unlock model concept with no pay-to-win mechanics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a complete playable Chapter 1 battlefield interface in `index.html`.
- Built canvas-rendered Normandy terrain, roads, hedgerows, buildings, walls, craters, objectives, units, and cover points.
- Added selectable Baker squad, Move/Attack/Suppress orders, tactical pause, speed controls, checkpoint, victory state, and enemy AI.
- Added cover and suppression indicators, health, radio traffic, objective progression, and restart behavior.
- Added responsive mobile and desktop layouts.
- Added a campaign dossier modal containing the 10-mission list, 3-act outline, controls, persistence, tech stack, and monetization guidance.
- Started a local server at port 3002 and confirmed it responds with HTTP 200.
- Created `game.js` with the extracted gameplay implementation.
- Confirmed that browser automation tooling is available.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked
- No visual verification screenshot was explicitly completed in the available state.
- Detailed C# pseudocode/architecture was not added to a separate source file.
- The planned canvas implementation still contains some refactoring duplication risk because `game.js` was only partially assembled from extracted code.

### Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete UI, styles, campaign dossier, and game integration entry.
- `game.js`: Canvas battlefield rendering and gameplay logic.
- `README.md`: Existing project metadata.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:3002` in a browser and verify the battlefield renders without console or script errors.
2. Complete `game.js` extraction/refactor so it fully contains all gameplay functions and is a canonical implementation.
3. Capture a desktop and mobile JPEG using the environment capture workflow.
4. Add a dedicated GDD/C# pseudocode document if the deliverables must exist outside the in-game dossier.
5. Test Move, Attack, Suppress, pause, checkpoint, objective capture, restart, and dossier interactions.

## Important Context
- The prototype uses a soft-real-time first mission: movement, enemy fire, suppression, checkpoint capture, and objective capture are playable.
- The campaign and tech/monetization requirements are represented in the dossier UI rather than in separate documentation.
- The implementation uses a canvas coordinate space of 1000 × 650 and is scaled responsively.
- A local HTTP server was started on port 3002.

## Objective
- Build a playable, mobile-first WWII real-time tactics campaign prototype with a polished first mission.
- Document the campaign concept, Unity architecture, and cover/suppression pseudocode.

## Requirements
- Company of Heroes-inspired campaign storytelling, touch-friendly controls, tactical pause, cover, suppression, and a 10-mission, 3-act campaign concept.
- Include fair monetization guidance and note assumptions.
- Save desktop and mobile screenshots for visual checks.

## Decisions
- Implemented a browser prototype in HTML/CSS/JavaScript rather than a Unity project.
- Assumed a fictional Normandy setting in June 1944; only Mission 1 is playable.
- Recommended a free first chapter and one-time full-campaign unlock, with no pay-to-win mechanics.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the playable battlefield UI and core mechanics in `index.html` and `game.js`.
- Added campaign dossier with mission list, story outline, controls, and field manual.
- Added `Campaign-Technical-Design.md` with the campaign outline, Unity implementation guidance, C#-style pseudocode, monetization, and prototype limitations.
- Fixed mobile layout ordering so the battlefield appears before the controls.
- Captured desktop and mobile screenshots in `screenshots/desktop.png` and `screenshots/mobile.png`.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` passes, the page responds over HTTP at port 3002, 10 missions render, and the dossier opens in browser automation.

### Active
- (none)

1: # The Long Road Home — Campaign & Technical Notes
2: 
3: ## Prototype scope
4: 
5: This repository contains a browser-playable vertical slice for Chapter 1, set near La Madeleine, Normandy, on 7 June 1944. The canvas prototype is a presentation and gameplay mock-up; it is not a Unity build. The dossier in the game summarizes the larger campaign and business model.
6: 
7: ## Campaign outline
8: 
9: A ten-mission, three-act story follows a platoon from the scattered aftermath of the Normandy landings through the Falaise pocket and toward a quiet farm. The central themes are the cost of survival, the bonds between veterans and replacements, and how ordinary people carry loss home. Radio exchanges, field-journal panels, mission events, and letters between chapters provide the narrative rather than long interruptions to play.
10: 
11: | # | Mission | Act / story beat |
12: |---|---|---|
13: | 1 | First light at La Madeleine | I — Regroup, hold the crossroads, and open a route for medics. *(Playable prototype.)* |
14: | 2 | The drowned lane | I — Find a missing element through flooded fields. |
15: | 3 | Letters from Sainte-Mère | I — Escort medics through a besieged village. |
16: | 4 | The orchard ambush | II — Survive a close-range ambush and identify its source. |
17: | 5 | A bridge in the dark | II — Reconnoiter and demolish a bridge before dawn. |
18: | 6 | Steel in the bocage | II — Coordinate infantry and armor in a costly duel. |
19: | 7 | The long retreat | II — Withdraw while protecting wounded soldiers and replacements. |
20: | 8 | Falaise road | III — Break through a congested, contested route. |
21: | 9 | No one left behind | III — Choose a rescue plan under severe time pressure. |
22: | 10 | The quiet farm | III — Reach safety, account for survivors, and read the names of the missing. |
23: 
24: Each mission targets 10–15 minutes, with a clear primary objective, optional tactical opportunities, a mid-mission checkpoint, and a short narrative debrief. The campaign concept carries surviving squad members, injuries, veterancy, and equipment forward. Fallen soldiers are remembered in the roster and story; they are not monetized or used as a retry penalty.
25: 
26: ## Unity implementation direction
27: 
28: For a production mobile/desktop game, use Unity with URP and a fixed-step simulation. Separate simulation state from rendering and UI so that tactical pause, save/reload, and deterministic replays do not depend on frame rate.
29: 
30: - **Mission layer:** authored objectives, triggers, reinforcement schedules, checkpoint snapshots, and narrative/radio events.
31: - **Squad layer:** finite-state machine (`Idle`, `Move`, `TakeCover`, `Engage`, `Suppress`, `Pinned`, `Retreat`, `Disabled`) with orders queued while paused.
32: - **Navigation:** NavMesh for traversable space, with a cover-point graph layered on top. Score candidate cover by protection, distance, approach cost, flanking exposure, and squad formation constraints.
33: - **Combat:** fixed-tick weapon resolution with range, line of sight, weapon accuracy, cover, suppression, and morale modifiers. Use a seeded random stream per mission for repeatable results.
34: - **Presentation:** URP lighting and restrained effects; UI Toolkit or uGUI for scalable HUD; input abstraction that maps touch, mouse, and controller to the same selection/order commands.
35: - **Persistence:** versioned campaign save containing mission checkpoint, squad roster, injuries, veterancy, gear, and completed objectives. Write atomically and retain a previous valid save.
36: - **Mobile performance:** pool effects/projectiles, cap simultaneous audio voices and particles, use LODs and baked lighting where practical, and profile on target devices before increasing battlefield density.
37: 
38: ### Cover and suppression pseudocode (C#-style)
39: 
40: ```csharp
41: void IssueMove(Vector3 destination)
42: {
43:     var candidates = coverGraph.Within(destination, searchRadius)
44:         .Where(point => navMesh.IsReachable(squad.Position, point.Position));
45: 
46:     var chosen = candidates
47:         .Select(point => new {
48:             Point = point,
49:             Score = point.Protection * protectionWeight
50:                   - PathCost(squad.Position, point.Position) * distanceWeight
51:                   - EnemyFlankExposure(point, knownEnemies) * flankWeight
52:                   - FormationPenalty(point, squad.Members) * formationWeight
53:         })
54:         .OrderByDescending(candidate => candidate.Score)
55:         .FirstOrDefault();
56: 
57:     squad.Order = chosen != null && chosen.Score >= minimumCoverScore
58:         ? SquadOrder.MoveToCover(chosen.Point)
59:         : SquadOrder.MoveTo(destination);
60: }
61: 
62: void TickSuppression(float fixedDeltaTime)
63: {
64:     foreach (var member in squad.Members.Where(member => member.IsAlive))
65:     {
66:         float incoming = combatEvents.SuppressionFor(member);
67:         float coverFactor = member.CurrentCover?.SuppressionFactor ?? 1f;
68:         member.Suppression = Mathf.Clamp01(
69:             member.Suppression + incoming * coverFactor
70:             - recoveryPerSecond * fixedDeltaTime);
71:     }
72: 
73:     if (squad.AverageSuppression >= pinnedThreshold)
74:     {
75:         squad.State = SquadState.Pinned;
76:         squad.CancelUnsafeAdvance();
77:         squad.AccuracyMultiplier = pinnedAccuracyMultiplier;
78:         squad.TryFindSaferCover();
79:     }
80:     else if (squad.State == SquadState.Pinned &&
81:              squad.AverageSuppression < recoverThreshold)
82:     {
83:         squad.State = squad.HasActiveOrder ? SquadState.Engage : SquadState.Idle;
84:     }
85: }
86: ```
87: 
88: In production, evaluate exposure from threat direction and line-of-sight rather than treating cover as a binary radius. Use hysteresis between pinned/recovered thresholds to prevent rapid state flicker, and communicate state changes through clear animation, audio, and HUD feedback.
89: 
90: ## Controls and fair monetization
91: 
92: The prototype supports tap/click selection, Move, Attack, Suppress, tactical pause (Space), speed controls, restart, and a campaign dossier. A full mobile release should provide generous touch targets, optional drag selection, and a command queue while paused.
93: 
94: Recommended model: a free first chapter followed by a one-time full-campaign unlock. Optional cosmetics may be offered if they do not obscure battlefield readability. No paid combat power, random paid rewards, energy timers, or purchasable retries.
95: 
96: ## Prototype assumptions and limitations
97: 
98: - Normandy in June 1944 is the assumed setting; characters and events are fictional and the story is not a representation of a specific real company.
99: - Only Mission 1 is playable. The rest of the missions, squad persistence, and checkpoint persistence are design targets, not implemented campaign systems.
100: - The current web simulation is intentionally lightweight: it uses simplified cover, combat, and suppression rules and does not contain Unity code or a real navigation mesh.
